final_message:
I wrote `answer.json` with four functions in `billing/subscriptions.py` that emit `subscription.updated` themselves:

- `subscriptions.transition` emits it for every status change except to `canceled`, where it emits `subscription.canceled`. It sets the event type in a variable, so a grep for the literal string finds it only once. Because of this, `pause`, `resume` and the dunning flow reach the event through `transition`. `dunning.record_failure` calls `transition` for `past_due`, and those callers don't emit it themselves, so I left them out.
- `subscriptions.change_items` emits it after replacing the items.
- `subscriptions.cancel` emits it when the cancellation is scheduled for the period end.
- `subscriptions.reactivate` emits it when it clears a scheduled cancellation.

Every other `emit` call in the package passes a literal event type. None of those literals is `subscription.updated`, so no other function emits it. I didn't run the tests or mypy, since I changed nothing except `answer.json`.

steps.command: cd billing; sed -n 30,200p subscriptions.py; grep -n "emit\|publish" *.py | grep -v "^subscriptions.py" | head -60

cd billing; sed -n 15,35p dunning.py; sed -n 20,32p refunds.py; sed -n 200,400p subscriptions.py | grep -n "emit\|^def " ; grep -rn "events\b\|emit" --include=*.py . | grep -v "emit(ctx, \"" | grep -v "^./subscriptions.py"
